body.statement: Using \(\mathrm{def:score-lifting-handle}\), can one prove for every base law \(P\) in the transported bounded likelihood-ratio joint chart that each \(s\in\mathcal C_P^\perp\) is an \(L^2(P)\) limit of finite linear combinations of scores of actual DQM paths \(t\mapsto P_t\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\) that remain in the bounded-ratio domain, with \(\sqrt{p_t}=\sqrt p(1+ts/2)+o(t)\), including moving kernels, genuine treatment-solvability, and the shared \((W,X)\) marginal, and hence that \(\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp\) for this actual restricted path class?
body.justification: This reverse inclusion remains the load-bearing open obligation for the actual bounded likelihood-ratio path class; neither operator perturbation nor differentiated solvability equations constructs the required paths.
body.gap: ChenSantos2018Overidentification and ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification give range-versus-annihilator arguments for outcome conditional moments, but not score lifting for the intersection of outcome and adjoint solvability loci with moving kernels and a shared marginal.
body.consumer: A positive answer determines the legitimate information bound for every regular estimator in the joint nonunique-bridge model.
